note: claude-opus-5-5、入力 3110 / 出力 2060 トークン

data.interpretation: The KPI has one main aim: maximize the number of orders delivered within the promised customer times, measured town-wide. Under the same seed the order count is fixed, so on_time_deliveries and on_time_rate rank amendments identically. It adds a fairness condition: no company's customers may be left behind. The KPI sets no numeric level for either aim, so no targets or guard values are set. The clause about proposing regulation revisions (invariants, quorum) when votes or the constitution block customer-friendly amendments is a process permission, not a metric. Any such proposal goes to the human and must state its effect on companies A, B, C and on customers.

options.label: Town-wide on-time count first, weakest company monitored

goals.text: Maximize town-wide deliveries made within the promised time (primary).
Monitor the on-time rate of the worst-off company so no company's customers fall behind.
Monitor orders left undelivered at period end, so late orders are not simply abandoned.

options.note: Follows the KPI's word order: volume first, fairness as a watched secondary. Uses the weakest company's rate rather than the gap, because the gap can be 'improved' by dragging the best company down. No levels are given, so no targets or guards are set.

options.label: Weakest company first, town-wide count monitored

goals.text: Raise the on-time rate of the worst-off company (primary).
Monitor town-wide on-time deliveries so fairness gains do not cost overall volume.
Monitor orders left undelivered at period end.

options.note: Reads 'leave no company's customers behind' as the binding priority. It may reject amendments that add many on-time deliveries but help only the stronger companies.

options.label: Town-wide on-time count first, company gap monitored

goals.text: Maximize town-wide deliveries made within the promised time (primary).
Monitor the spread between the best and worst company on-time rates.
Monitor late deliveries so orders that miss the promise are still delivered rather than dropped.

options.note: Reads fairness as equality between companies. The gap can shrink when the best company gets worse, which is why option 1 is preferred.

concerns: Volume and fairness can conflict: an amendment may add town-wide on-time deliveries while lowering one company's rate. The KPI does not say which wins, or by how much a company may fall behind. Without a stated level, fairness can only be monitored, not enforced as a guard.

'Leave no company's customers behind' can be read as protecting the weakest company (min_company_on_time_rate) or as equality (on_time_rate_gap). The gap is a risky proxy because it improves when the best company gets worse.

Counting only on-time deliveries rewards deprioritizing orders that are already going to be late. Those orders could end up unfinished, which hurts customers. Unfinished or late deliveries should be watched.

Relaxing the promised times in DELIVERY_SLA would inflate on-time counts without real service gains. Contract changes affect customers, who do not vote, so they must be decided by the human, never adopted to hit this metric.

Regulation revisions (invariants, quorum) are permitted to propose but are always decided by the human. Each proposal must state how companies A, B, C and customers are affected. In particular, lowering a quorum removes a company's ability to block changes that harm it, which may conflict with the fairness aim.
